We break up the integral as follows:

$$
{\int }_{-\infty }^{\infty }\frac{2x}{{x}^{4}+9}\,\text{d}x={\int }_{-\infty }^{0}\frac{2x}{{x}^{4}+9}\,\text{d}x+{\int }_{0}^{\infty }\frac{2x}{{x}^{4}+9}\,\text{d}x.
$$

First, we calculate the antiderivative using a substitution. Let  $u={x}^{2}$,  then $\text{d}u=2x\text{d}x.$ Hence,

$$
\begin{aligned}\int \frac{2x}{{x}^{4}+9}\,\text{d}x & =\int \frac{1}{9+{u}^{2}}\,\text{d}u \\  & =\frac{1}{3}\operatorname{arctan}⁡\frac{u}{3}+C \\  & =\frac{1}{3}\operatorname{arctan}⁡\frac{{x}^{2}}{3}+C.\end{aligned}
$$

We now evaluate the first of the improper integrals, as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}{\int }_{-\infty }^{0}\frac{2x}{{x}^{4}+9}\,\text{d}x & ={lim}_{a\to -\infty }{\int }_{a}^{0}\frac{2x}{{x}^{4}+9}\,\text{d}x \\  & ={lim}_{a\to -\infty }{(\frac{1}{3}\operatorname{arctan}⁡\frac{{x}^{2}}{3})|}_{a}^{0} \\  & =-{lim}_{a\to -\infty }(\frac{1}{3}\operatorname{arctan}⁡\frac{{0}^{2}}{3}-\frac{1}{3}\operatorname{arctan}⁡\frac{{a}^{2}}{3}) \\  & =-{lim}_{a\to -\infty }(0-\frac{1}{3}\operatorname{arctan}⁡\frac{{a}^{2}}{3}) \\  & =0-\frac{\pi }{6} \\  & =-\frac{\pi }{6}\end{aligned}
$$

Now, notice that the integrand is an **odd** function. This means that we can immediately deduce that 

$$
{\int }_{0}^{\infty }\frac{2x}{{x}^{4}+9}\,\text{d}x=\frac{\pi }{6}.
$$

Therefore, since both improper integrals exist, we conclude that 

$$
\begin{aligned}{\int }_{-\infty }^{\infty }\frac{2x}{{x}^{4}+9}\,\text{d}x & ={\int }_{-\infty }^{0}\frac{2x}{{x}^{4}+9}\,\text{d}x+{\int }_{0}^{\infty }\frac{2x}{{x}^{4}+9}\,\text{d}x \\  & =-\frac{\pi }{6}+\frac{\pi }{6} \\  & =0.\end{aligned}
$$
